Digital Creativity I · I.2 2D drawing tools

Exercise 1 · Croquis proportion scaffold

Draw the scaffold alone first. Place landmarks before contour. Garment finish waits on a separate layer.

Label the practice before you name the file — JPEG never answered a venue.

(Tao of the Image)

Scaffold layer + garment layer pair; one sentence on the landmark that locked the pose.

Image: CosmicBloom.jpg

CosmicBloom · Unknown · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Source

  • Timer: 20 minutes. Individual. ACT1 figurín craft (proportion), not a second graded channel.
  • Choose a head-count or grid scaffold and draw it alone first.
  • Place landmarks (shoulder, waist, hip, knee) before contour.
  • Trace a second pass for garment only on a separate layer.
  • Compare scaffold vs finish; mark one collapsed decision.

Source: Classroom adaptation (croquis / Abling page cite held).

Ask: Which landmark would break first if you changed medium?

Digital Creativity I · I.2 2D drawing tools

Exercise 2 · Three alternatives, then construction vs finish

Make three visibly different silhouette versions. On the winner, colour-code construction lines vs finish — hide finish and ask a peer what still reads.

The phone gives us a lot but it takes away three key elements of discovery: loneliness, uncertainty, and boredom.

(Kleon 2019)

Three versions + scoring sheet + construction/finish audit on the winner + one defence paragraph.

Image: Work in Progress.JPG

Work in Progress · Photograph uploader on Commons · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Source

  • Timer: 25 minutes. Individual + one peer check.
  • Make three visibly different versions of the silhouette. Score novelty and fit (1–5); rank and defend the winner.
  • On the winner: colour-code construction lines vs finish lines.
  • Hide finish; ask a peer what garment they still understand.
  • Restore finish only where it adds information. One sentence: which line type carried the silhouette.

Source: Classroom adaptation for the three-alternative drill; critical frame that imagination ≠ creativity ≠ fantasy (Hüppauf and Wulf 2009, 32) — do not treat “more finish” as “more creative.”

Ask: Did your rarest alternative also carry the clearest construction?
